sources.title: Davide Gaiotto, Gregory W. Moore, and Andrew Neitzke, Spectral Networks

contents.name: Class-S spectral curve, sheet-pair trajectories, finite webs, geometric charge lifts, and framed surface-defect data

source_review.read_extent: Retrieved the complete arXiv v2 PDF (87 pages) and inspected the complete relevant passages in §2, §§3.1–3.3, §§4.1–4.4, §§5.1–5.2, and §§9.2–9.3, including equations (2), (3)–(9), (23)–(24), and the soliton-data definition.
source_review.supports: The type-A class-S spectral curve, the sheet-difference trajectory equation and orientation, absolute and relative charge lifts, genericity of the framed interface, and the trace conventions for soliton and framed BPS indices.
source_review.limitations: The physical class-S construction and Hilbert sectors are supplied model data; the precise charge lattice may be a subquotient of H1. The authors note the sign-lift subtlety and do not fully quantize general finite-web zero modes.

contents.name: Source-qualified limit on deriving numerical indices or wall-crossing identities from a geometric network alone

source_review.read_extent: Inspected the complete relevant introduction and §3.1 passages on finite webs and second-helicity indices, including the source's qualification of its geometric wall-crossing argument.
source_review.supports: The item states that numerical BPS indices require model-supplied Hilbert sectors and that geometric data alone do not prove a physical index identification.
source_review.limitations: The source says general finite-web zero-mode quantization is incomplete and calls its wall-crossing argument 'if not quite a proof'; it is not used as a proof of finite-field or universal physical wall crossing.

contents.name: T3 cubic differential, canonical torus cover, branch-point coordinates, and slope convention

source_review.read_extent: Retrieved the complete arXiv v1 full-text HTML and inspected the relevant full proofs/passages in §2.1 and §3.1, the T3 rational-slope definitions and formulas, and Appendix A's phase-convention comparison.
source_review.supports: The normalized differential, equilateral torus cover, ramification points A/B/C, and the exact slope/determinant convention for (p0,q0)=(2,1).
source_review.limitations: The flat normalization is geometric; no scale in this calculation is identified with a physical mass without a supplied model normalization.

contents.name: The projected saddle connection is a finite web and its canonical lift has nonzero geometric central charge

source_review.read_extent: Inspected Definition 2.4, the complete canonical-lift construction, the complete proof of Lemma 2.7, and the T3 network theorem/proof in §3.3.
source_review.supports: The finite metric-ribbon-graph criterion, canonical lift to H1, and phase/nonvanishing result; the local item additionally computes the selected one-edge period directly.
source_review.limitations: The source theorem is geometric and does not quantify a 4D Hilbert space or compute a numerical BPS or framed index.

contents.name: Abstract physical interpretation of the T3 cubic differential

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete relevant abstract and introduction passages identifying the physical interpretation and the scope of the T3 study.
source_review.supports: The source's qualified description of the cubic differential as a geometric building block for type-A2/SU(3) theories.
source_review.limitations: No physical charge quotient, BPS state, defect index, or numerical index value is imported from the abstract; the item keeps each such identification conditional.
